beats.say: Here is a small test image, and here is one noisy measurement of it.
beats.caption: Here is a small test image, and here is one noisy measurement of it.

beats.say: Every pixel value got random noise with a standard deviation of 0.25, on a scale from 0 to 1.
beats.caption: Every pixel value got random noise with a standard deviation of 0.25, on a scale from 0 to 1.

beats.say: If we can take many measurements, can we get the clean image back?
beats.caption: If we can take many measurements, can we get the clean image back?

beats.say: The bottom row shows what is left: the error, at its true scale. It fades as the copies add up.
beats.caption: The bottom row shows what is left: the error, at its true scale. It fades as the copies add up.

beats.say: Measured over 20 trials, the error falls from 0.25 to 0.125, 0.0625, and 0.031.
beats.caption: Measured over 20 trials, the error falls from 0.25 to 0.125, 0.0625, and 0.031.

beats.say: That is the noise divided by the square root of the number of copies. Four times the copies, half the error.
beats.caption: That is the noise divided by the square root of the number of copies. Four times the copies, half the error.

beats.say: But this only works when the noise in each copy is independent.
beats.caption: But this only works when the noise in each copy is independent.

beats.say: When copies share half their noise, correlation 0.5, the error stops near 0.18, even with 64 copies.
beats.caption: When copies share half their noise, correlation 0.5, the error stops near 0.18, even with 64 copies.

beats.say: The shared part never averages out. Its floor is 0.177, and averaging cannot go below it.
beats.caption: The shared part never averages out. Its floor is 0.177, and averaging cannot go below it.
